newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon drops plan to increase farm export taxes.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon drops plan to increase farm export taxes.

text.p: Cameroon's government has scrapped a plan to raise export tax payable on a series of agricultural products from July 1, according to a new presidential decree.
The reason for the change was not immediately clear.

The new decree, dated April 28 and just made public, overrides an April 21 decree raising the tax on cocoa, cotton, sugar, rubber and medicinal plants to 15 percent of the FOB value from 13.5 percent.
The April 21 decree proposed raising the export tax on coffee to 25 percent of the FOB value, and on palmoil to 30 percent, in both cases also from 13.5 percent.
The new decree, however, did not affect a cut from July 1 in the levy on fresh bananas to 4,000 CFA francs per tonne from 6,500.

These export taxes were first levied in 1994 after the devaluation of the CFA franc, with the government taking advantage of competitive gains realised by agricultural groups as a result of the parity change.
